pr_body:
Adds support for `Array#intersection` to `Style/ArrayIntersect`. 

Since [`Array#intersection`](https://ruby-doc.org/2.7.8/Array.html#method-i-intersection) allows for more variation than `Array#&` (ie. it can have zero or multiple arguments), the cop only considers it if given exactly 1 argument.

Fixes #13986.

* [x] Added an entry (file) to the [changelog folder](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/changelog/) named `{change_type}_{change_description}.md` if the new code introduces user-observable changes. See [changelog entry format](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entry-format) for details.

pr_comments: I did notice that `Array#intersection` with 0 args behaves like `dup`. Not sure why they left such an arity when normally you'd need at least 2 arrays for their intersection, so I thought for a moment we might discourage it with some cop... probably an overkill, though.

issue_context.title: `Style/ArrayIntersect` should also detect `.intersection`
issue_context.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

`Style/ArrayInterection` does not detect use of `.intersection`:

```ruby
foo.intersection(bar).any?
```

## Describe the solution you'd like

Cop should detect above case.

## Additional Context

```
rubocop -V
1.73.2 (using Parser 3.3.7.1, rubocop-ast 1.38.1, analyzing as Ruby 3.2, running on ruby 3.4.2) [arm64-darwin24]
```

review_comments:
`good` examples may simply be moved. i.e.,:

```
      # @example
      #   # bad
      #   (array1 & array2).any?
      #   (array1 & array2).empty?
      #   (array1 & array2).none?
      #
      #   # bad
      #   array1.intersection(array2).any?
      #   array1.intersection(array2).empty?
      #   array1.intersection(array2).none?
      #
      #   # good
      #   array1.intersect?(array2)
      #   !array1.intersect?(array2)
```
